name: Four Seasons Scottsdale at Troon North
insider_take: Perched dramatically against the legendary Pinnacle Peak with the vast Sonoran Desert stretching endlessly beyond, this Four Seasons feels more like a private desert compound than a hotel – where every casita is positioned to capture those legendary Arizona sunsets that paint the sky in impossible shades of copper and gold.
whats_special: This resort sits on 40 pristine acres within the exclusive Troon North community, home to two of Golf Digest's top-rated desert courses. The property's unique positioning at 2,400 feet elevation means cooler temperatures and crystal-clear desert air. Each of the 210 casitas features private terraces with unobstructed views of Four Peaks, Pinnacle Peak, or the resort's stunning desert landscape. The spa incorporates authentic Sonoran Desert elements, including treatments using locally-sourced jojoba and prickly pear, while the resort's signature restaurant sources ingredients from local desert farms and Native American communities.
pro_tip: Book a casita on the north side for the most dramatic Pinnacle Peak views, and time your arrival for late afternoon – the desert light show begins around 4 PM and the resort's elevated position offers some of the Valley's most spectacular vantage points for Arizona's famous sunsets.
dont_miss: The resort's signature Desert Walk with the resident naturalist reveals hidden petroglyphs and teaches you to identify the calls of roadrunners and coyotes. The Troon North Golf Club's Monument Course features the famous "Tombstone" hole, carved through a natural rock formation. For the ultimate desert experience, book the private stargazing session on the resort's helipad – Scottsdale's dark sky designation means you can see the Milky Way with remarkable clarity, and the concierge can arrange for a professional astronomer to guide you through constellations that ancient Hohokam peoples once used for navigation.
pros: World-class golf resort with two championship Troon North courses
Stunning Sonoran Desert setting with mountain views
Exceptional Four Seasons service and luxury amenities
Award-winning spa and multiple dining venues
cons: Premium luxury pricing reflects high-end positioning
Desert location may be too remote for some guests
